subject: Clarifying scope: FinTrust evidence request for data erasure and retention controls
messages:
From: Jack Foster <jack.foster@fintrust.com>

Cc: security@fintrust.com, Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@fintrust.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Evidence package for data deletion of PII test set

Hi Priyom,

During our SOC 2 readiness review we flagged a short list of items under retention/disposal. We need a compact evidence package for the small PII test set Redwood processed for our proof-of-concept (POC) last year: specifically deletion confirmation, traceability of the deletion job, and confirmation that derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) were either removed or are covered by retention exceptions.

Deliverables we can accept: log of deletion job, S3 manifest showing objects removed, KV/DB snapshots showing TTL or tombstone markers, and a short note on how embeddings are handled. If you have a one-page compliance statement mapping artifacts to SOC 2/ISO controls that would help.

Can you confirm scope and turnaround? We need this for our auditor by 2026-04-20.

Thanks,
Jack
Jack Foster
Head of Information Security, FinTrust

[Attachment: fintrust-evidence-request-20260411.pdf]

Hi Jack — thanks for the clear list. Confirming receipt and timeline: we can produce a focused packet by 2026-04-14 EOD PT with the items you listed. A couple quick clarifications so we scope exactly the artifacts you need: 

- Which datasets/IDs should we target? I assume the POC dataset labeled FT-POC-2024 in your intake, but confirm if there are additional buckets or prefixes.
- Do you need cryptographic proof of deletion (hash-to-erase) or operational logs and manifests suffice for your auditor?
- For embeddings: do you require proof that vector records were deleted from the vector store and any derived indexes removed, or is a signed attestation acceptable?

Looping in Marcus for the technical artifacts and Kimberly and Lauren for compliance language and packaging.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Evidence package for data deletion of PII test set

Hi team — technical summary below that I can include in the packet. I'm also attaching the raw deletion job log and the S3 manifest we produced when the job ran on 2026-04-12.

Key points (technical):
- Target: S3 objects with prefix s3://redwood-prod/fintrust/ft-poc-2024/ (confirmed by audit flags).
- Deletion process: scheduled batch job triggered deletion across region-us-west-2; job id deljob-2026-04-12-FT001. The job performs object DELETE API calls, then writes a manifest of object keys removed.
- Durability/replication: objects were deleted from the primary region; we also issued cross-region deletion for replicated copies in eu-west-1. See manifest (s3-deletion-manifest-fintrust-20260412.csv).
- KV/vector store: vectors stored in our Redis-backed vector-index (namespaced fintrust_ftpoc). Deletion implemented via tombstone + async compaction. Snapshot (kv-ttl-snapshot-2026-04-12.csv) shows keys flagged with tombstone=1 and compaction job id comp-2026-04-12-09.
- Logs: deletion-job-2026-04-12.log includes API responses, job checksums, and job completion timestamp.
- Derived artifacts: model cache entries and embeddings used for fast routing are TTL'd; we removed the POC namespace and kicked the compaction. For the auditor, I can produce a short script output showing zero vectors for the namespace after compaction.

Attachments: deletion-job-2026-04-12.log, s3-deletion-manifest-fintrust-20260412.csv, kv-ttl-snapshot-2026-04-12.csv

Let me know if you want me to redact any internal request ids before sending to FinTrust.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Team — adding compliance framing to match SOC 2 / ISO language so FinTrust's auditor can map artifacts directly. Draft text below I propose to send as a one-page mapping. Please review and flag anything inaccurate.

Draft compliance mapping (one-page):
- Control family: Data Retention & Disposal (SOC 2 CC6.1 / ISO 27001 A.8.3)
- Scope: Objects under s3://redwood-prod/fintrust/ft-poc-2024/ and associated vector namespace fintrust_ftpoc processed during the POC (April 2024).
- Evidence included: deletion-job-2026-04-12.log (operational job record with timestamps and API responses); s3-deletion-manifest-fintrust-20260412.csv (list of object keys deleted, including bucket, key, size, timestamp); kv-ttl-snapshot-2026-04-12.csv (KV/vector namespace markers showing tombstone entries and compaction job id); DocuSign proof of request/authorization (doc-sign-proof.pdf).
- Residual risk/notes: backups retained under our backup retention policy are stored on WORM-protected medium; per policy automatic retention sweep excludes recent POC artifacts after receiving a formal erasure request (we executed an expedited retention purge for FT-POC-2024). We will provide a statement and a timestamped snapshot of backup indexes that shows the absence of FT-POC-2024 pointers (redaction available on request).
- Assertion: Redwood performed deletion actions and cross-region replication clean-up on 2026-04-12. Technical artifacts and signed attestation provided.

If everyone signs off I will convert to PDF and include a short cover note referencing SOC 2/ISO control IDs. Lauren, can you add the business approval line and final packaging steps?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
